messages:
aj: Heads-up — spotted a perf regression after yesterday's kernel-chooser tweak when running Mistral-8x7b with our sliding-window attention config. P95 token latency on >1k sequences increased ~18-22% on several runs.

sofia: ugh. which path is switching? sliding -> dense or dense -> sliding? :thinking_face:

aj: The chooser is favoring the 'scanline' optimized kernel for many batches now (it matched short seq perf), but for long sequences the scanline kernel has worse memory access patterns for our KV tiling and ends up thrashing the cache. We see more memcpy/epochs in the profiler.

ben: can you paste the perf snippet? also was this only on 8x7b or on 7b too?

aj: Only obvious on 8x7b so far. Snippet from perf: 
```
kernel_selector: chosen=scanline_opt_v2
seq_len=1200 batch=8
GPU kernel time breakdown:
  scanline_gemm       5.4ms (prev 2.2ms)
  kv_copy_overhead    1.8ms (prev 0.6ms)
  ropescale_adjust    0.9ms
CPU: increased scheduling stalls ~12%
```

maggie: that scanline variant does extra per-head packing to avoid warp divergence. For 8x7b with our head/kv dims it might be doing too many small kernels. Could be kernel granularity mismatch.

sofia: interesting — we also noticed a RoPE scaling tweak in the same rollout (reduce scale by 0.98 for numeric stability). Could that interact?

aj: Possibly. The ropescale path adds a short kernel that touches KV, and with scanline packing it forces an extra sync. Alone it's tiny, but combined with the memcpy churn it's tipping tails.

nate: I ran a microbench: toggling RoPE scaling back to 1.0 removes the extra 0.9ms ropescale_adjust kernel, but total P95 still ~10% higher vs baseline. So both chooser and ropescale matter.

ben: Any regression in correctness/outputs or only perf?

aj: Outputs look fine. But we see subtle attention mask quirks when max_position_embeddings isn't aligned with our batch slicing — some token offsets end up with a different mask pattern causing the sliding window fallback to use a conservative mask that disables some KV cache shares. That's causing more cold-KV hits.

maggie: that explains increased kv_copy_overhead. If mask alignment causes smaller prefix shares, we lose effective cache locality. Can you repro with an explicit mask that mimics ideal alignment?

aj: Yes — when I force the ideal mask the kv_copy_overhead drops back to ~0.7ms and p95 gap narrows.

sofia: action items then: (1) revert chooser heuristics for long-seq threshold, (2) patch kernel to avoid extra sync when ropescale is a no-op, (3) add a guard to ensure mask alignment when slicing batches for sliding-window, (4) add microbench in CI for 7b/8x7b long seqs.

ben: +1 on CI microbench. Also we should add a telemetry metric: kernel_choice + seq_len histogram to detect this earlier.

nate: I can open a quick PR for the chooser revert + metric. Will include a small benchmark harness (1200/1600 seq) to run on our perf rig.

aj: Thanks — I'll prepare a repro script and attach profiler captures. For now roll the rollout back on prod pools with reserved 8x7b capacity? infra-bot: rollback job queued for pool:redwood-prod-8x7b at 3m ETA.

maggie: one more note — our tiled KV layout for 8x7b uses head_size=64, kv_dim=128 per-tile. The scanline kernel assumes contiguous KV per head; if our tiling scatters across pages the L2 miss rate jumps. We should evaluate a lightweight re-layout when scanline is selected.

sofia: good catch. Let's track: CH-#4523 (chooser rollout regression) with sub-tasks for kernel patch, mask guard, telemetry, and CI microbench.

aj: I'll drop the perf traces into CH-#4523. If anyone can triage the kernel sync point (maggie/ben), that would be great.

ben: will do. posting preliminary notes in the issue in 20m. :eyes:

infra-bot: deployment rollback completed for pool:redwood-prod-8x7b at 2154322048. 

aj: confirming: metrics trending back to baseline on the rolled back pools. thanks team. :thumbsup:
